subject: Embeddings latency degradation after catalog change — ACME
messages:
From: Sasha Bloom <sasha.bloom@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform-ops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:12:03 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p95/p99 after morning catalog push

Jonas —

We just observed a sharp degradation in embeddings latency starting ~07:45 PDT this morning, right after your team's model catalog update. Our ingestion pipeline (batched vectors) is seeing p95 climb from ~120ms to ~480ms and p99s up to ~1.8s; error rate for the /embeddings route also increased from 0.2% -> 1.6% (transient 429s). This is impacting our semantic search queries and a handful of user-facing features.

I attached a small perf dump and a screenshot of our SLO dashboard. Can you confirm whether anything in the catalog change could have affected routing or a model variant? We're mid-launch and need a fast mitigation plan.

—Sasha
Sasha Bloom
VP, Platform
Acme Corp

Attachment: perf_dump_20270915.json (perf trace, ~120KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Bloom <sasha.bloom@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:25:41 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p95/p99 after morning catalog push

Hi Sasha — thanks for the heads up and for the dump. Really sorry you're seeing this. I'm looping in Monica (Customer Success) and Neha (Infra on-call) to take it straight to the ops runbook.

Immediate plan:
- Neha to triage live routing and isolate whether traffic hit a new catalog variant (ETA 15m).
- If we detect a bad variant, we'll roll traffic back to last-known-good model within 30 minutes and confirm SLOs.
- We'll follow with a short postmortem and proposed credit for the incident window.

Do you want us to proceed with an automatic rollback if we confirm the model-tag mismatch? Please confirm — we'll only roll back with your approval unless you tell us to proceed.

Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:33:02 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: sudden jump in embeddings p95/p99 after morning catalog push

Folks — forwarding Acme's dump and SLO screenshot. Quick observations from our side:
- Customer reported p95 -> ~480ms, p99 ~1.8s; matches our backend telemetry for the embeddings service between 07:45-08:05 PDT.
- No increased queueing on the ingress layer, but a noticeable increase in per-token generation CPU time for the embeddings workers that started at the same timestamp as the catalog deploy.
- ACME is a high-throughput customer for this route; they're seeing transient 429s during peak batches.

Asking infra to confirm model variant mapping and the catalog audit logs (+1 on rollback if needed). I've pre-opened INF-5483 and attached a short summary.

-Monica
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo_dashboard.png

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:46:50 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden jump in embeddings p95/p99 after morning catalog push

Triage update (quick):
- Confirmed: catalog rollout at 07:40 PDT introduced model tag "embed-v3-experimental" into routing for the hosted embeddings route in us-west-2.
- The experimental variant is a quantized build that missed a KV-cache warmup patch; because of that, cold-starts for many short-batched requests showed increased per-request latency (p95/p99).
- Logs (excerpt):
  [2027-09-15T07:45:12Z] route=embeddings host=embed-worker-45 model=embed-v3-experimental kv-cache=miss token_time=6.2ms
  [2027-09-15T07:46:07Z] route=embeddings host=embed-worker-12 model=embed-v3-experimental kv-cache=miss token_time=5.9ms
- No resource exhaustion observed (CPU and memory within expected). This points to a model runtime behavior change.

Recommendation: immediate rollback of the model tag mapping for embeddings to the previous stable variant (embed-v3-stable) while we backport the warmup fix. Rollback path is tested and should complete within 12 minutes.

I'll open a runbook action: revert-catalog-mapping -> monitor 10 minutes -> validate p95/p99. Marcus/Stephanie can you prepare the canary checks and customer-facing SLO report?

-Neha
Infra On-call

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Bloom <sasha.bloom@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:58:14 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden jump in embeddings p95/p99 after morning catalog push

Sasha — quick status update and request:

- We confirmed the catalog mapping included an experimental variant (embed-v3-experimental) deployed at 07:40 PDT.
- Neha recommends rolling traffic back to embed-v3-stable; rollback path is verified and estimated to finish in ~12 minutes.
- If you approve, we'll execute the rollback now and follow with a 10-minute monitoring window; if SLOs recover we'll keep you posted and open a postmortem with timeline and remediation steps.

If you prefer we can keep both variants and throttle the experimental for a staged ramp, but given the customer impact we recommend immediate rollback. As an apology for the disruption we'll propose a credit covering the affected window — I can draft the credit terms once we resolve.

Please reply "proceed" to authorize rollback; otherwise we'll wait for explicit approval.

—Jonas

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Sasha Bloom <sasha.bloom@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: rollback complete — embeddings SLOs recovered

Update — rollback executed at 09:10 PDT and validation completed.
- Timeline: rollback triggered 2027-09-15T09:10:23Z, traffic fully shifted back by 09:22Z.
- Post-rollback SLOs: p95 dropped back to ~130ms within 5 minutes; p99 back under 260ms after 10 minutes. Error rate returned to baseline.
- Root cause (initial): catalog mapping allowed an experimental quantized model variant without KV-cache warmup to receive production traffic.
- Next steps: INF-5483 assigned for a patch to the model build (warmup behavior) and an additional catalog gating check to reject variants that lack required warmup metadata. We'll schedule a joint postmortem and publish timelines to ACME.

Jonas — I'll prepare the customer-facing incident note and a proposed credit draft. Monica, can you sync with ACME on postmortem timing?

Attachment: slo_recovery_snapshot.png

-Marcus Lin
Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
